title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Chapter II of the 1986 notes builds topological realizations of 'réseaux' (networks, i.e. combinatorial cell structures such as maps or graphs on surfaces). For this he needs a purely topological notion of a codimension-one 'wall' A in a space X along which X can be cut. The previous page sets up the vocabulary:
- Ã → A is the space of local sides (local branches) of X−A along A. When A is regularly immersed, X̃ is a compactification of X−A whose boundary is Ã, like a real oriented blow-up or the complement of an open tubular neighbourhood.
- Riv(A,X), the 'rivières', is the Boolean ring (an idempotent F2-algebra) of germs of clopen pieces of X−A near A. It maps to the components of Ã.
- A 'bivière' is a complementary pair {ρ,ρ'} with ρ+ρ'=1, equivalently a splitting Ã = Ã1 ⊔ Ã2. A 'locally disconnects' X if a non-trivial bivière exists.

This page: definition of a 'maille' (mesh) with 'nœud' (node) A. The crossed-out first try was 'bande marginale' (marginal band). A bivière {Ã1,Ã2} defines a maille structure on X with node A when:
- A (corrected over the line to: the side space Ã, or its iterate) is regularly immersed in X. Then it is regularly immersed in X̃, and so are Ã1 and Ã2.
- The pair (X̃,{Ã1,Ã2}) satisfies conditions a) b) c) of a 'feuille topologique' (topological sheet) from earlier pages. It is a genuine sheet if Ã is regularly immersed in X̃.

Construction. Form the iterated pushout X̄ = X̃ ⊔_{Ã1} A ⊔_{Ã2} A, gluing each side back onto its own copy of A. Call it Dec_β(A,X), 'X cut open along A'. Here β = {ρ,ρ'} is the two-element set of sides (margin: 'le binaire'). Then:
- X̄ contains two disjoint closed parts A_ρ and A_ρ', each canonically isomorphic to A; together they form A×β.
- There is a canonical map X̄ → X restricting to a homeomorphism X̄ ∖ (A×β) → X∖A.
- On A×β it is the projection to A, so each A_ρ → A is a homeomorphism.

The next page goes on to:
- require (X̄,{A_ρ,A_ρ'}) to be a topological 'recollement';
- define an orientation of a maille as a choice of one side (rive) ρ;
- start a compatibility condition for two mailles (A1,β1), (A2,β2), illustrated on an annulus with two cuts.

In short, this is the standard 'cut a space along a two-sided codimension-one subspace' construction, made axiomatic and intrinsic. The two-sidedness datum is encoded as a splitting of the Boolean algebra of local sides, presumably so that cell complexes or maps can later be glued and cut functorially.
errors: No real error. For X̄ → X to be a homeomorphism off A×β, and for A_ρ, A_ρ' to be disjoint copies of A mapping homeomorphically, one implicitly needs each Ãi → A to be a surjective quotient map. In the intended case they are homeomorphisms; otherwise the pushout copies of A carry no relation to the local sides. This is presumably what the 'feuille topologique' conditions a) b) c) ensure, but that is not stated on this page.

The self-correction in the regular-immersion hypothesis (A vs Ã vs a double-tilde) is left unclear. The parenthetical deduction 'then it is regularly immersed in X̃, hence so are Ã1, Ã2' only makes sense for the side space Ã, not for A itself.

ideas.what: Boolean ring Riv(A,X) of germs of clopen pieces of X−A near A ('rivières'); a bivière as a complementary pair, i.e. A locally separating X into two sides
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of local components / ends of the deleted neighbourhood; two-sidedness / local separation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical point-set topology (Freudenthal ends, local separation theory, Wilder)

ideas.what: Maille with node A: a regularly immersed codimension-1 subspace together with a chosen bivière, satisfying sheet-type conditions
ideas.modern_name: two-sided (bicollared / locally flat) codimension-one subspace; wall in a cellular stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in geometric topology (bicollar theorems: Brown 1962)

ideas.what: Dec_β(A,X) = X̃ ⊔_{Ã1} A ⊔_{Ã2} A: cutting X open along A, giving two copies A×β and a map to X that is a homeomorphism off A×β
ideas.modern_name: cutting along a two-sided hypersurface (as in Haken hierarchies, real oriented blow-up followed by collapsing the side boundaries)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (3-manifold topology, Haken; real blow-up: A'Campo and others)

ideas.what: Orientation of a maille as a choice of side (next page)

missed.claim: This is an axiomatic, intrinsic (stratification-free) framework for cutting and regluing spaces along two-sided walls. The two-sidedness datum is encoded as a splitting of a Boolean algebra of local sides. It serves to give topological realizations of combinatorial 'réseaux' (maps / cell complexes), in the spirit of the tame topology of the Esquisse. The mathematics itself is standard; what is unrecorded is Grothendieck's specific 1986 attempt and its vocabulary (rivière, bivière, rive, maille, nœud, Dec_β).
missed.quote: on trouve un espace X̄ = Dec_β(A, X), avec deux parties (indexées par β) canon. isom. à A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only: it documents how Grothendieck tried to found a 'topologie modérée' for dessins and maps via cut-and-paste axioms. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine definition of cutting a space along a two-sided codimension-one subspace, with idiosyncratic terminology. It has historical value as part of the 1986 réseaux / tame-topology project, but contains no mathematics that a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Margin at the Dec line reads approximately 'β={ρ,ρ'} le binaire': β is the two-element set of sides {ρ,ρ'}, not '{β,β'}'.
The two parts of X̄ are written {A_ρ, A_ρ'} in the image (and 'A_ρ ∪ A_ρ'' under the brace), not A_β, A_β'.
The final lines read 'et des homéomorphismes A_ρ ≅ A, A_ρ' ≅ A, i.e. la projection canon. A×β → A'.
'Considérons' is partly struck out or overwritten at the start of the pushout line.

The marginal word next to the bracketed condition is 'vérifiant'. The corrected hypothesis line appears to read 'Ã est régulièrement immergé dans X̃...' with a double tilde overwritten. It is uncertain whether the object is Ã or a double-tilde A.
